ARABIC — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.

2. When practising Speaking Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency.

3. When practising Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Imitative speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Imitative speaking.

4. When practising Selective Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening.

5. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Only memorise without using the language
   B. Avoid speaking to classmates
   C. Mix random languages with no purpose
   D. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

6. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.

7. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.

8. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.

9. When practising Conversational skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Conversational skills.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational skills.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Conversational skills.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational skills.

10. When practising Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Conversational skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Selective Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Independent Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
